stem.en: Which statement best explains how having no cell wall suits animal tissues?

text.en: Animal cells are too small to carry a wall around their membrane.

feedback.en: Bacteria are much smaller than animal cells, and they have walls.

text.en: Animal cells are never in contact with water, so they do not need one.

feedback.en: Animal cells have water on both sides of their membranes.

text.en: A wall made of cellulose would stop all the water from entering them.

feedback.en: A cell wall is permeable, so it would not stop water.

text.en: Their cells can change shape, which supports movement.

explanation.en: Without a rigid wall, animal cells can change shape easily, and this flexibility supports the movement and working of animal tissues.

hints.en: What can a cheek cell do that an onion cell cannot?
